mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing consumer and business spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate declines but S&P 500 forward returns remain negative or flat in 20 days, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 4% but S&P 500 returns remain positive, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates stronger demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase by more than 5% but S&P 500 returns remain negative or flat, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests stronger supply-side activity, which may lead to increased economic output and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases by more than 2% but S&P 500 returns remain negative or flat, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong GDP growth and low inflation suggests a favorable economic environment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is strong and inflation is low but S&P 500 returns remain negative or flat, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate combined with slowing GDP growth may indicate monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate is above 5% and GDP growth is below 2% but S&P 500 returns remain positive, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll employment growth suggests a robust labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If payroll employment grows by more than 1% but S&P 500 returns remain negative or flat, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales suggests stronger consumer demand, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If retail sales increase by more than 3% but S&P 500 returns remain negative or flat, this hypothesis is invalidated.
